utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would firstly like to be sure that I ask the photographers to wait for a moment - that the technical equipment is working. Does everybody hear me? The Registry? The Defence? The Office of the Prosecutor? Assistants? Colleagues? Turning to the Registrar, would you please call the case number which is on the agenda for today and for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case IT-96-22-T, this Tribunal against Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Turning again to the Registrar, would you please have the accused brought in? The photographers have now left the room. I would first like the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor to identify himself. Who is representing the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I am Eric Ostberg. I appear today with my fellow senior trial attorney, Mr. Mark Harmon.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: I am Jovan Babic, an attorney from Yugoslavia, the Defence attorney for the accused Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Erdemovic, would you rise, please? For the Tribunal, would you state your name, your first name or names, the place and the date of your birth, your profession at the time that you were arrested and your profession before the acts that you are being charged with today by the International Criminal Tribunal. We will now hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: My name is Drazen Erdemovic. I was born on 25th November 1971. I am a locksmith. I did not have any work experience. I was in the war - I was in the army during the war because the war broke out and I was in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please indicate where you were born and what your nationality is?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I am a Croat, a Bosnian Croat, by nationality and I was born in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. This hearing is a sentencing hearing which means that it is designed for a sentence to be handed down against the accused Drazen Erdemovic. I recall that this person pleaded guilty to the charge of crime against humanity during his initial appearance on 31st May 1996. I also recall that the Trial Chamber ordered on 31st May and on 4th July 1996 that two psychological and psychiatric evaluations be performed in order to be sure, first, that the accused had the ability to know what he was doing at the moment that he pleaded guilty and to be sure at the same time that the accused is competent to stand trial. I would now like to ask the Registrar to recall the relevant texts dealing with the hearings which would lead to a sentence before this International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. More specifically, I would like the Articles having to do with the accusation of crime against humanity and the relevant Articles having to do with the methods for understanding what sentence should be handed down be read. I give you the floor, Mr. Marro.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 5A of the Statute of the International Tribunal, crime against humanity: "The International Tribunal shall have the power to prosecute persons responsible for the following crimes when committed in armed conflict whether international or internal in character and directed against any civilian population; (a) murder". Article 24 of the Statute, penalties: "The penalty imposed by a Trial Chamber shall be limited to imprisonment. In determining the terms of imprisonment, the Trial Chambers shall have recourse to the general practice regarding prison sentences in the courts of the former Yugoslavia. (2) In imposing the sentences, the Trial Chambers should take into account such as the gravity of the offence and the individual circumstances of the convicted person". Rule 101 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, penalties: "(A) A convicted person may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term up to and including the remainder of his life. (B) In determining the sentence, the Trial Chamber shall take into account the factors mentioned in Article 24(2) of the Statute, as well as such factors as (i) any aggravating circumstances; (ii) any mitigating circumstances including the substantial co-operation with the Prosecutor by the convicted person before or after conviction; (iii) the general practice regarding prison sentences in the courts of the former Yugoslavia, and (iv) the extent to which any penalty imposed by a court of any state on the convicted person for the same act has already been served, as referred to in Article 10(3) of the Statute".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marro. The purpose of the hearing today (and perhaps tomorrow as well) is to allow the Prosecutor on the one hand and on the other the Defence to present all information which might be relevant which would allow the Trial Chamber to decide what would be the most appropriate sentence for Mr. Erdemovic. Under these circumstances, the Trial Chamber has decided that it would organise the hearing in the following fashion. First, the Prosecutor will recall the facts and the accusation, that is, the accusation and he will bring in the witness or witnesses that he wishes to call before the Trial Chamber. In the second place, so that the proceedings in which both parties are present are respected and that there be no ambiguity having to do with the acts which have been admitted, the Trial Chamber will hear, still referring now to the acts and the charges, the answer of the Defence as exposed or as presented by the Prosecutor, so that the possible witness or witnesses can be heard in this respect. After these presentations and testimonies, the Trial Chamber reserves the right, pursuant to the powers that it has, to order the production of additional evidence which is given to it by Rule 98 of the Rules. Therefore, it preserves the right to hear other witnesses, including the accused, should that appear to be necessary for the Trial Chamber. Following that, the closing arguments will be heard during which the Prosecutor will be asked to present all of the aggravating circumstances or any mitigating circumstances and any other circumstances, mitigating or attenuating, pursuant to the texts which have just been read and any other facts which appear relevant in support of his position, including his suggestions having to do with the appropriate sentence, if the Prosecution does, of course, wish to make any proposals to the Trial Chamber. The Defence will respond to the same questions, that is, aggravating or mitigating circumstances and any suggestions that it wishes to make to the Trial Chamber. Last, the Trial Chamber will deliberate in order to reach its decision. Therefore, before we give the Prosecutor the floor, the Trial Chamber would first like to ask both of the parties, that is to the Prosecution and to the Defence, whether they agree that the words that Mr. Erdemovic stated in which he reiterated his plea of guilt during the status conference which was a closed one be made public during this hearing. I recall that on 4th July the Presiding Judge of this Trial Chamber asked Mr. Drazen Erdemovic, so that things be absolutely clear, to repeat his plea of guilt. The status conference was closed and, therefore, I now ask the Prosecutor and Mr. Babic whether they agree to the Registrar reading the passage of that status conference. I turn to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I have no objection at all to that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: I also have no objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Turning to the Registrar, would you please read what was read during 4th July in which the Presiding Judge asked Drazen Erdemovic whether he planned to continue to plead guilty to the charges of which he was accused? THE REGISTRAR: The Trial Chamber composed of Judge Claude Jorda presiding, Judge Elizabeth Odio Benito and Judge Fuad Riad, status conference, Office of the Prosecutor, Eric Ostberg and Mr. Mark Harmon and Terri Bowers and Mr. Babic, counsel for the Defence. I am referring to page 7 of the transcript in French. Presiding Judge: "I am now going to turn to Drazen Erdemovic. Could you rise, please? Do you still plead guilty in this trial?" Drazen Erdemovic, interpretation from Serbo-Croat: "Yes". The Presiding Judge: "I would like the Registrar to record this in the records because, according to the medical evaluation, Mr. Drazen Erdemovic is confirming that he is pleading guilty in this trial".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. The second question is the following: do the parties plan to bring any evidence? If so, I would like this evidence to be presented to the Trial Chamber. Are there any objections on the part of the Defence or of the Prosecutor of the other side giving any other evidence? Do you have any evidence that you wish to present to the Trial Chamber, Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, we do, your Honour. We have just one witness, Mr. Jean Rene Ruez, who is the investigating officer of the Office of the Prosecutor into taking statements from Mr. Erdemovic and to conduct the investigations on the site of the events.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not get an interpretation there. I heard you but I did not get the interpretation. It is preferred for the interpretation to give us a faithful translation or interpretation, excuse me, of what you said. Can we begin again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would it not be too disagreeable for you to repeat what you just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: We are going to bring just one witness, Mr. Jean Rene Ruez, who is going to testify on the statements he has been taking from Mr. Erdemovic and the investigation he has been conducting in the site of the events with which we charge Erdemovic. This is the only oral evidence we are bringing. Then we are bringing other evidence in the form of photos, diagrams and maps of the place where these events took place. That will be all the evidence produced from the side of the Prosecutor, besides, of course, your Honour, the two briefs we have already filed with you on the sentencing system of the former Yugoslavia and the mitigating and aggravating factors. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This evidence, therefore, will be delivered to the Trial Chamber Judges at the time that Mr. Jean Rene Ruez testifies, if I have understood correctly. Turning to Mr. Babic, have you yourself any evidence that you would like to submit to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not opposed to having Mr. Ruez heard as a witness. On the other hand, as I had proposed previously too, I suggest that we hear as witnesses before this Court the witnesses who are under protection, the two witnesses that are under protection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am asking you right now whether you had any evidence, which evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The final point before we give the floor to the Prosecutor is that before we supplement any protection for witnesses X and Y who have been mentioned by the Defence, we have been asked that there be a 30 minute delay in the transcription - that the images will not be distributed for 30 minutes so that the complete protection of witnesses X and Y will be assured.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I support that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: I agree. THE PRESIDING JUDGE: Therefore, under these conditions the deliberations have now been organised properly by the Trial Chamber. As has just been recalled by the Legal Officer, there will be an order written for this. It will be given to the Registrar, the agreement of the parties and the order according to which we will have a 30-minute delay in the broadcasting and of the images. Without any further ado, we will now move to the first sequence which has to do with the recall of the facts and the accusations, only the facts and the accusations. I would, therefore, like to now give the floor to the Prosecutor who will himself decide whether this is the proper time to bring in his witnesses, but always now speaking about the facts and the accusations, the floor will now be given to the Defence. It is only after that that the Trial Chamber will come to a decision as to whether or not other witnesses should be heard or whether the accused should be heard, that is, Drazen Erdemovic. I now give you the floor, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Before I start presenting the facts of the case, I will give a brief summary of the events that brought Mr. Erdemovic into the custody of the Tribunal in The Hague. It takes us back to the attack by the Bosnian-Serb Army under the command of Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic on the safe area of Srebrenica in the beginning of July 1995, and the surrender and executions of thousands of Bosnian Muslims that fled Srebrenica through the woods towards Muslim territory in Tuzla. These events resulted in investigation, indictments and Rule 61 hearings within this Tribunal. The authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia also started an investigation into Drazen Erdemovic's involvement in these events which led to his arrest on 2nd March 1996 in Serbia. Having been informed thereof, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal considered that Drazen Erdemovic appeared to be in possession of information related to the indictment against Karadzic and Mladic, and made an application for his transfer to The Hague as a witness. Pursuant to an order to that effect by Judge Riad, Erdemovic arrived in The Hague on 30th March 1996. In connection particularly with the statements given by Erdemovic to investigators of the Prosecutor's Office, the Prosecutor instituted an investigation into Erdemovic's participation in the execution of the aforementioned surrendered people. This investigation led to the indictment against Drazen Erdemovic. It was confirmed on 29th May 1996 by Judge Sidhwa and an order was issued by him on the same day to arrest Erdemovic in the case. On the same day of 29th May 1996, a Trial Chamber of the Tribunal decided to request the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to defer all the investigations and proceedings against Erdemovic to the Tribunal. Erdemovic's initial appearance, as the President just mentioned, took place before this Trial Chamber on 31st May 1996 at which time he pleaded guilty to the acts charged against him as a crime against humanity under Article 5 of the Statute of this Tribunal. On 5th July he appeared as a witness in the Rule 61 hearing against Karadzic and Mladic and told this Trial Chamber about his participation in the executions of Muslim men at the Branjevo farm near Pilica town and what he then saw in Pilica in Zvornik municipality in Bosnia. His accounts of the events included descriptions of the killing he perpetrated. Now, after having Erdemovic's mental health thoroughly examined, we have reached the point in time for a sentence hearing in accordance with Rule 61 and Rule 100 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. It is my task now to present to your Honours the facts that constitute the charges against Drazen Erdemovic. I can think of no better and comprehensive way of doing that than to cite the words of the indictment which in relevant parts I now want to read: "On 16th April 1993, the Security Council of the United Nations, acting pursuant to Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter, adopted resolution 819, in which it demanded that all parties to the conflict in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina treat Srebrenica and its surroundings as a safe area which should be free from any armed attack or any other hostile act. Resolution 819 was reaffirmed by resolution 824 on 6th May 1993 and by resolution 836 on 4th June 1993. On or about 6th July 1995, the Bosnian Serb Army commenced an attack on the UN 'safe area' of Srebrenica. This attack continued through until 11th July 1995, when the first units of the Bosnian-Serb Army entered Srebrenica. Thousands of Bosnian Muslim civilians who remained in Srebrenica during this attack fled to the UN compound in Potocari and sought refuge in and around the compound. Between 11th and 13th July 1995, Bosnian-Serb military personnel summarily executed an unknown number of Bosnian Muslims in Potocari and in Srebrenica. Between 12th and 13th July 1995, Bosnian Muslim men, women and children who sought refuge in and around the UN compound in Potocari were placed on buses and trucks under the control of Bosnian-Serb military personnel and police and transported out of the Srebrenica enclave. Before boarding these buses and trucks, Bosnian Muslim men were separated from Bosnian Muslim women and children and were transported to various collection centres around Srebrenica. A second group of approximately 15,000 Bosnian Muslim men, with some women and children, fled Srebrenica on 11th July 1995 through the woods in a large column in the direction of Tuzla. A large number of the Bosnian Muslim men who fled in this column were captured by or surrendered to Bosnian-Serb Army or police personnel. Thousands of Bosnian Muslim men who had been either separated from women and children in Potocari or who had been captured by or surrendered to Bosnian Serb military or police personnel were sent to various collection sites outside of Srebrenica including, but not limited to, a hangar in Bratunac, a soccer field in Nova Kasaba, a warehouse in Kravica, the primary school and gymnasium of 'Veljko Lukic-Kurjak' in Grbavci, Zvornik municipality and diverse fields and meadows along the Bratunac-Milici road. Between 13th July 1995 and approximately 22nd July 1995, thousands of Bosnian Muslim men were summarily executed by members of the Bosnian- Serb Army and Bosnian Serb police at diverse locations including, but not limited to, a warehouse at Kravica, a meadow and a damn near Lazete and diverse other locations. On or about 16th July 1995, Drazen Erdemovic and other members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment of the Bosnian-Serb Army were ordered to a collective farm near Pilica. This farm is located north west of Zvornik in the Zvornik municipality. On or about 16th July 1995, Drazen Erdemovic and other members of his Unit were informed that bus loads of Bosnian Muslim civilian men from Srebrenica, who had surrendered to Bosnian Serb military or police personnel, would be arriving throughout the day at this collective farm. On or about 16th July 1995, buses containing Bosnian Muslim men arrived at the collective farm in Pilica. Each bus was full of Bosnian Muslim men, ranging from approximately 17 to 60 years of age. After each bus arrived at the farm, the Bosnian Muslim men were removed in groups of about 10, escorted by members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment to a field adjacent to farm buildings and lined up in a row with their backs facing Drazen Erdemovic and members of his Unit. On or about 16th July 1995, Drazen Erdemovic did shoot and kill and did participate with other members of his Unit and soldiers from another Brigade in the shooting and killing of unarmed Bosnian Muslim men at the Pilica collective farm. These summary executions resulted in the death of hundreds of Bosnian Muslim male civilians". This, your Honours, concludes my reading of the facts which are stated in the indictment. I just want to add some few things, namely, that the act described in the indictment was a part of a widespread and systematic attack launched by the Bosnian-Serb Army on the safe area of Srebrenica and its inhabitants. To substantiate the allegations of the indictment, to demonstrate the details of Erdemovic's participation in the executions and to inform the Court of the extent of Erdemovic's co-operation with the Prosecutor's Office, the Prosecution will bring just one witness which I named just before, namely, Jean Rene Ruez who is, as I said, the officer who took the statements and did the investigations. During this examination of the witness, the Prosecution will also present as evidence maps, diagrams and photos from the area. I will conclude this statement of facts by adding that prior to the account of the events in that area voluntarily given by Drazen Erdemovic, the Prosecutor's Office had no knowledge whatsoever about these events. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostberg, I have a question I would like to ask you: do you plan, since you have just re-read this indictment which we all know, to bring in your witness, Mr. Jean Rene Ruez, immediately? Do you plan to bring him in immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Therefore, before we give the floor to the Defence, we will ask the Registrar to have the witness for the Prosecution brought in, that is, the investigator John Rene Ruez, making it clear that Mr. Ruiz will speak about the facts and about the accused's participation in the acts for which he has been charged. MR. JEAN RENE RUEZ, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am afraid not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Could we do something, Registrar? Do you hear me now? The Registrar should see to it that we do not have problems of this kind, I believe. You can hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So please stand and read the solemn oath, please. Do you have the wording there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I solemnly declare that I shall tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You have the floor, Prosecutor. Examined by MR. HARMON

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. The purpose of calling Mr. Ruez is three-fold; the first is to have Mr. Ruez summarise the events relating to the takeover of the UN safe area of Srebrenica in July 1995. The second purpose is to have Mr. Ruez describe to this Trial Chamber two events, two massacres, that occurred, one at Pilica farm, and the other that occurred at a cultural centre in the village of Pilica - two events which Mr. Erdemovic brought to our attention. The third purpose of having Mr. Ruez testify is to have him describe to this Trial Chamber the substantial co-operation of Mr. Erdemovic with the Office of the Prosecutor. Prior to having Mr. Ruez testify, I have asked that the Registrar office premark 15 exhibits. I would now ask that usher pass from the Registrar's Office to Mr. Ruez a set of those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, with regard to the Chamber's decision as to how we were going about this, I think Mr. Jean Rene Ruez will first answer your questions concerning the first two points, that is to say, summing up the events, the general background as regards what happened in Srebrenica and then also the massacre at the farm and at the culture centre in Pilica. Thereafter, Mr. Jean Rene Ruez will remain available, and it is only during the second go through when we go into the aggravating and mitigating factors, because it is in that light that we have to consider the co-operation with the OTP and it is at that point we will ask him to return to this courtroom. So, I would ask that for the time being we stick to the summary you mentioned and to the massacres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. There is one Exhibit also that I would ask the usher to bring in. It is a large map. I would ask him to kindly place it on the easel that is to Mr. Ruez's left. Mr. Ruez, we will proceed in the manner in which Judge Jorda has requested. Therefore, let me ask you first to state your name and spell your last name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is John Rene Ruez, RUEZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, prior to coming to the Office of the Prosecutor, can you tell me what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since '86 I have been a superintendent in France.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you describe your duties and responsibilities since arriving at the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have worked at the Office of the Prosecutor investigators since April 1995 and at the time I participated in the investigation in connection with the siege of Sarajevo. Since July '95 I have been in charge of investigating the fall of the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, using Exhibit No. 2 which is before you, would you please summarise for the Court what your investigation has shown with regard to the events in Srebrenica? Could we please have Exhibit No. 2 shown on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, the events fall into a general context following the fall of the enclave in July '95, to sum up briefly, because all of this has already been heard in connection with the Karadzic and Mladic hearing in July of this year -

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have a question - excuse me - for the Prosecutor: you submitted to the Chamber the transcript of the hearings we heard in connection with Rule 61 against Messrs. Karadzic and Mladic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will submit to the Chamber, your Honour, the Rule 61 testimony of Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, because Mr. Ruez was just saying that as this is known. No, these are two distinct cases. There is a link, of course, in terms of the takeover of the Srebrenica enclave, but I do think we have to make quite clear what happened in Srebrenica. Either the Prosecution asks that be submitted to the Chamber all of the information that would be deemed relevant, in particular what Mr. Erdemovic said and, in particular, in connection with the Rule 61 hearings against Mladic and Karadzic, or Mr. Jean Rene Ruez, on the contrary, should go into something a lot more detailed about Srebrenica. If I have understood rightly, Mr. Harmon, you are going to lodge the transcript of the Rule 61 hearings that were held in July of this year in connection with the Mladic and Karadzic case, and today you are going to proceed towards a summing up of what happened in Srebrenica, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do apologise, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, when the Bosnian-Serb Army took Srebrenica, the people there had two possibilities, one was to flee towards Potocari, the second option (which is the option followed by most of the men) that was to escape towards Tuzla through the countryside. The men who stayed at Potocari and the women and children there were deported to Kladanj. That was on the borderline, as it were, with the Serb Republic. A lot of murders were committed in respect of the men at Potocari. That is here on the chart. Now, on the way to deportation, a number of men did manage to get on buses. They were all removed from the convoys at various points. The final point of their separation was at Tisca and from there they were also taken and executed nearby. Now, those who fled through the woods had to, on account of the action taken against them, either to surrender or they were taken prisoners. Now, in a great number of situations that we were told about, the people who surrendered were executed on the spot. Most of them were grouped together in the following days, that is to say, on 12th and 13th July 1995. At the collection points which are in Sandici and Nova Kasaba, but there were also other points, there was executions carried out as well. Now, some executions were mass executions. The prisoners who grouped at Sandici were taken into a compound in Kravica. They were placed in a hangar and they were all executed in that hangar. Other executions took place at the crossroads at Konjevici, also at Nova Kasaba where there were regroupments of people. Men were killed in groups of ten. In the Cerska Valley, individuals taken prisoners were transported and executed there as well. Now, this list is but a summing up of all the places where executions took place. Most of the men were grouped in the city of Bratunac. That is true of those who stayed in Potocari as well as those who had tried to escape through the woods. Now, from Bratunac the prisoners were taken to various places.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, excuse me, there were also those who tried to flee towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are the ones I am talking about now.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Because it is not perfectly clear. You said that there were two options and, if I have understood you rightly, people both in the column towards Tuzla and those who had left towards Potocari were involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the men from Potocari were grouped together at Bratunac, except those who managed to get on buses and then they were separated out later at some checkpoints between Bratunac and the confrontation line. Now, when all of the survivors were brought together at Bratunac, further crimes were committed against them, including at Bratunac itself. But subsequently they were all transported to various other points more to the north of the enclave. Several of these places have been identified, in particular, the school at Grbavci which is on the map here - [The witness indicated] - at that point. The prisoners were grouped together at that school at Grbavci and were executed at a site called Lazete which is nearby, and there has been some excavation work done this summer. Others were taken up to the Petkovci school which is a little bit further north. This is the green spot on the map here. Now, those who were grouped together at Petkovci school were subsequently executed next to the Dulici dam. This is north of the Zvornik. Others were taken to the Pilica school. Now, on the basis of what was said, it was at the Branjevo farm that the executions take place which is nearby. Here, let me show you on the map. It is right there. [The witness indicated]. Then, lastly, others were grouped in a public building in Pilica and they were executed there. So that is the general overview of the events subsequent to the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I would like you to describe to the Court what occurred at Pilica farm and, in so doing, would you refer to any exhibits that have been marked and are before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here again I will sum up the statements made by Drazen Erdemovic on this matter on several occasions. 16th July, in the morning, when he was at Drasnica(?) at the base of his Unit, Drazen Erdemovic went as part of a group of eight individuals at Zvornik. The head of the Unit was in touch with the Lieutenant Colonel who was coming out of a building that was occupied by the military police - was identified on that by Drazen Erdemovic in a photo. It is part of the Drina Corps, the Unit involved. Now, not informed of the day's mission, they followed this Lieutenant Colonel who took them to the farm, the farm referred to as the Branjevo farm where the Lieutenant Colonel gave orders to the head of the Unit to leave, and Drazen Erdemovic was informed by this individual that buses would be coming with prisoners from Srebrenica. He had understood then what the purpose of operation was and that he would be involved in the execution of these people. The buses started arriving at 10.00 in the morning, approximately. On the whole, some 60 buses were seen, according to Mr. Drazen Erdemovic, by the 20 buses, excuse me, these buses had about 60 prisoners in them and until 3.00 in the afternoon the executions took place at that farm. Now, thanks to the information provided by Mr. Erdemovic, we could go to the site in question. Let me refer to Exhibit 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you mean -

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Exhibit 3, the interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is Exhibit 3. Here you have a photograph of the farm. Mr. Erdemovic has seen this and he has identified it as being the place where the executions took place that day. Now, when we went here near the site we found some clothing, shoes, human debris, in other words, things indicating that a mass grave might be located nearby. Now, a subsequent mission enabled us to gather from the field where the execution took place a number of cartridges. Only 61 cartridges were found because the soil had been worked on. There was still agricultural activity there, so we found the cartridges that were on the surface. There were only 61 of them, but that certainly does not indicate that not many more were fired than that there. Now, I would also like to refer to Exhibit 4. On the basis of the information provided by Mr. Erdemovic -

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you wait a minute until we get this in focus, Mr. Ruez? All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The basis of Drazen Erdemovic's information, the relevant services could look and in the archives could find pictures which had been taken near the time the events took place, so we could have access to these pictures. This was from 17th July 1995. This is a bird eye's view of the farm, and you can see a number of bodies scattered over the field and there is a probable mass grave there in the process of being dug. I would now like to refer to Exhibit 5.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecutor, could we dim the lights a bit? It is hard for us to see what is on the screen. So if the lights could be dimmed, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, using these kind of images, we were also able to find some traces of what is an attempt to destroy evidence at the Branjevo farm. Now, this is a photo dated 27th September 1995 and there there are some traces of work underway at the site. This is as of 27th September '95. Now, the acts as reported by Drazen Erdemovic are confirmed by the findings here, in particular, by the shell cases where they were found. There has been an exhumation that took place in late August and early September, exhumation work, and despite the work seen here 153 bodies were found at the spot where work is underway on this aerial photograph. So 153 bodies were found in this area. About half of those bodies had their hands tied. There were some further cartridges that were found as well as some ID. It was Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica area who were involved. Now, it is far too early to draw any definitive conclusions as regards the exhumation work from July, so I will not say anything on that. There is still work underway. Now, it is worth mentioning that the events as set forth by Drazen Erdemovic about this farm were not known to the Prosecutor at the time. There are a large number of victims involved and that is significant because Drazen Erdemovic said some 1,200 people were killed there and the site is 70 kilometres north of Bratunac which, of course, does have a significant impact for the investigation in terms of the logistics that were involved for this execution to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me turn your attention, because I think you are getting into an area that I would like to reserve, that is, how Mr. Erdemovic has assisted the Prosecutor's Office in its investigation, to the cultural hall in Pilica and ask you to describe and summarise what occurred at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are referring to the public building at Pilica, so we are no longer talking about the farm?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, this is still on 16th July (and I will be summing up Drazen Erdemovic's statements made in the course of a number of hearings), now about 3.00 in the afternoon when the executions were over at the Branjevo farm, the Lieutenant Colonel who had been there, been in charge since Zvornik, he asked the Unit Drazen Erdemovic belonged to to participate in the execution of 500 prisoners who were locked in a public building at Pilica. Drazen Erdemovic states that he refused to participate in the second execution and his colleagues did likewise. The Lieutenant Colonel, all the same, gave the execution squad a meeting in a cafe in the village of Pilica. Other individuals who were there and who were involved in the execution along with Drazen Erdemovic's Unit immediately went there. While Drazen Erdemovic was still at the Pilica farm, he could already hear the firing and the explosions taking place - it sounded like grenades exploding - and the firing was taking place near the farm.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The farm and the public building, are they nearby, near one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they are close enough for such sounds to be heard. Now, along with the members of the firing squad, they went to the aforementioned cafe which was opposite a building, in the building which the people were held prisoners, and he could see that other members of the Bosnian-Serb armed forces were in the process of the executing people who were locked inside that building. He did not have access to the building. He did not see what was going on inside the building, but he could hear the firing. He saw the individuals throwing grenades and he saw some prisoners who were trying to escape and who were shot down outside the building. Now, when that execution was over, the group that had carried it out went into the cafe and the group Drazen Erdemovic belonged to immediately left. Now, a number of conclusions could be made subsequent to Mr. Drazen Erdemovic's statements about the acts as described. Exhibit 6 - I do not see it on my screen, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we also have the lights dimmed, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After we had the details which Erdemovic gave us and which we were able to verify, this photograph which is the photograph of the cafe in which Drazen Erdemovic was when he was the witness to the executions, this is a photo which was given to him and which he recognised. For Exhibit No. 7, this photograph shows what Drazen Erdemovic could see from the cafe that is of the building in which the executions were being carried out, the other side of the street which goes to Janja in Zvornik. Exhibit 8 shows a sign that was on the building where we can read "Socialist Republic of Bosnia- Herzegovina, Assembly of the Zvornik municipality. Local office, Pilica". It, therefore, means that this was a public building. Exhibit 9 shows the front of the building. This part is the place where the prisoners were locked up and this is the door going in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, were these photographs taken by members of the Office of the Prosecutor as a result of the information provided by Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the photographs which I am now showing you, having to do with these events, were taken by myself and the photograph which has the No. 9 was taken by Peter Nicholson who is also a member of the Office of the Prosecutor. On this photograph we can see the inside of the building, the building in which the executions are alleged to have taken place. The definition of the image is not very good, but inside the building there were traces of bullet impacts which can be seen on all the walls, on the ground and on the platform. Exhibit No. 10 - no, I am sorry, it is 11, shows the impact traces as well as blood traces near the stairs which led up to the podium. Exhibit 12 is an example of the traces which can be seen on the walls, the walls of the room. These are traces of blood with bits of hair as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see anything on the ceiling of the building as well, Mr. Ruez, when you were at the site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the ceiling which is about four metres high was also splattered with all kind of substances probably from human beings, but for which the analysis has not yet been completed. Exhibit 13 is a view of the back of the room behind the podium. Certain parts of that podium have been destroyed because it appears that there were grenade explosions there, but traces which are still being analysed but which do seem to be traces of powder, of explosions, which were on the walls as well traces of blood and human remains which can be seen on the walls. A later mission for analysis of the site was carried out in September and a complete study of the place was done by the crime technicians. We do not yet have the results, but we can already state that all of the statements made by Drazen Erdemovic have been confirmed by the observations which we were able to carry out on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes my examination of Mr. Ruez on the two points, the summary of the events at Srebrenica and a description of the Pilica farm and the hall in the village of Pilica. I have no further questions of him on those points.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Prosecution. I would like now to turn to Mr. Babic and ask the following question: having to do with the facts only, all of these facts which have just been recalled by the Office of the Prosecutor, through the indictment on the one hand and on the other hand through Mr. Ruez's testimony, I myself and my colleagues would like to know what is your feeling?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the indictment issued against the accused Drazen Erdemovic is based exclusively and only on the basis of his voluntary statement, statements that he gave to the authorities in Yugoslavia, to the authorities of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia and the statements that he gave before this honourable Trial Chamber. In relation to that, I am perfectly sure that while respecting the principle of directness of giving testimonies, it is most useful that the accused Erdemovic, Drazen Erdemovic, gives his testimony once again before this Trial Chamber in order he can give a direct statement in order he can tell why he feels guilty for what he did, because his confession is also his defence. According to the findings of experts, he is perfectly capable to do this today and he should take this opportunity. The accused Drazen Erdemovic is not a man who wanted, who wished, to do something like that. I have called certain witnesses here, witnesses X and Y, and I would like the Trial Chamber to hear their testimony before Drazen Erdemovic's testimony. As for the statement of Mr. John Rene Ruez, I have just two or three questions, if you will allow me to do so, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber grants you leave to ask questions after which the Judges will also ask questions, a few questions that is, of the witness after which we will suspend the hearing. After the adjournment, we will first decide whether we are going to hear the accused and, in the second place, whether we are all going at that point of the hearing to hear the witnesses which you would like to bring in. If I have understood you correctly on this last point, the witnesses whom you wish to call in and who are covered, as I recall to you, by protective measures, and at the proper moment I will ask the Registrar to recall those measures, they have been in place, that is, because of the desire of your client not to participate in these events. Therefore, I feel it would be better to start with the sequence of the sentencing trial, the sentencing hearing, which has to do with what we were talking about, these particular circumstance, do you agree, because these witnesses did not actually participate in the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Therefore, we will give you an answer to that. For the time being, however, Mr. Babic, unless we were to take a break at this point, and I can now turn to my colleagues. (The learned Judges conferred)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, you can ask your questions after which the Tribunal will ask its questions and we will have our break after that. I now give you the floor to ask the questions that you wish to ask. Cross-Examined by MR. BABIC

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: My first question is in relation to the testimony, if I have properly understood, of Mr. Jean Rene Ruez in which he indicated - it is about Pilica - that, according to statements given by witnesses in the field, I would just like to ask the following: does it mean that he talked to witnesses who knew about the crime from a direct testimony in Pilica, and if there have been such witnesses, can he tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour -

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: That is my first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: - I would in respect of the -

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: First let us be clear. This is a question which is addressed to Mr. Ruez, but there is an objection on the part of the Prosecutor. What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My objection is to the identity of any direct witnesses because it is important for the Prosecutor's Office not to reveal the names of other direct witnesses to these events. We would object to Mr. Ruez identifying them by name. We have no objection to his indicating whether or not such witnesses exist, however.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We accept the objection of the Prosecutor. I think the interest of your question really has to do with whether these have to do with the testimonies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will have to broaden the framework somewhat. The first point having to do with these witnesses is that the statements of Drazen Erdemovic allowed us to show the connection between what had taken place as described by the witnesses and the only thing which - at the time the only thing that we knew for sure is that they had been shut up in the Pilica school. Had we had not the information from Drazen Erdemovic, we would not probably have been able to make the connection between the place of the detention and the place of their execution which was close by. As regards the way the execution took place and the way that Drazen Erdemovic explained the facts, in fact, both of the statements in general confirmed one another which is significant -

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that when you say the two statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way which the surviving witness of an execution which took place near the Pilica school and which is probably the same as the one that Drazen Erdemovic described, both events resemble one another very closely. But at this point of the investigation we cannot yet say for sure that the survivors were the victims of the same execution in which Drazen Erdemovic was involved. This is still being investigated. A detail which should be important to understand is that Drazen Erdemovic does seem to be convinced that the buses that were bringing in the victims to the Branjevo farm had come from Zvornik. The Pilica farm is near the Pilica school and, although the final approach road is the same as the one that goes from Zvornik or from the school, he does not confirm that those prisoners who were executed in the Branjevo farm were the ones who had been detained at the Pilica school, but he knew about this. But the way things took place was very similar.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So do I understand, therefore, that in order to answer this question very clearly which is of interest to the Tribunal that you heard survivors testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Turning to the Office of the Prosecutor, these testimonies, even if they are distorted or are not revealed, are you planning to give these testimonies to the Tribunal, even if you are not going to reveal the names and other identifying material?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We were not intending to do so, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I must state, Prosecutor, that I am somewhat surprised because we have just heard from John Ruez's mouth and from your own that the investigation is still going on, and also that you have other testimonies. I do understand, as far as they are concerned, that it would be important to protect them, but I think that while protecting them we have enough resources which would allow us to hide their identifying material but to keep the substance of the testimonies, even if they were only through a summary that you would give us. This is a question which I will deliberate over with my colleagues because I do believe we are now trying a man, and I believe that the Tribunal cannot simply accommodate itself with the idea of knowing that there is an investigation in process and at the same time that there are witnesses whose testimonies have not been made available to the Tribunal. We do understand that the witnesses must be protected, but the Tribunal cannot judge a man about whom it is said that in the Prosecutor's case files there are testimonies which are significant, and which the Tribunal is not aware of. This is what I wanted to say to you. Do you agree? Could you make a suggestion to the Tribunal about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am perfectly capable of making a suggestion to the Court, your Honour. After the recess, if I could have some time to consult with Mr. Ruez and investigators and my colleagues, I would be prepared to answer your question directly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of course, Prosecutor, you will make the suggestion after the pause. I thank you and I now can give the floor back to Mr. Babic so he can ask his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: I have understood the answer. There have been several witnesses and testimonies of those witnesses who were concordant to the testimony given by the accused Drazen Erdemovic. My next question would be, Mr. Ruez said that at the very site of the crime after the testimony of Erdemovic certain traces were found, shoes, body parts, parts of clothes and so on, and that the exhumation established the existence of 153 bodies whose hands were tied and some other traces, such as bullet cases and so on. I would like to know whether Mr. Ruez or his team who worked on the site of the investigation have composed some kind of a report from their on-site investigation. Has there been any photo documentation, photo file or video file that was established after the investigation? Has there been any kind of technical expertise, technical analysis, of the traces found on the spot in the cultural hall that we saw on the monitor? If, yes, what are the results of their analyses? What we have heard here, has it been confirmed in their analyses? This concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the operations about which we are now speaking, all the technical operations, all those that were carried out recently, today no report has yet been given to us by the experts who may be responsible for carrying out this work. The only thing that can be stated right now, having to do with the results, is that in general they confirm the events as they were described by Drazen Erdemovic, but no detailed conclusion can yet be drawn. I would certainly allow myself to say this, in so far as these are experts in the field who have been made responsible for the process, and it is a process in which I was not involved, I would like to make a correction of something which was just stated by Mr. Babic having to do with the number of bodies. The number I have given is an approximate figure. The number of bodies has still not been determined since some body parts are difficult to attribute to one or another individual and, therefore, the figure, 153, remains an approximate one.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will now allow myself to turn to the Defence, and would like to ask a question: you do not intend to bring into question your client's plea? You do not plan to change that, do you, or to raise questions about it? Because you have just asked a question which is one of the Tribunal, because the Tribunal has the right to ask the questions and it will do it. But here, for not only those that are listening to us, but all of those parties involved in the case, understand what I am saying, you pleaded guilty. The role of the Tribunal through all of the investigations and all the questions it will ask during these two days for its own intimate conviction will be to corroborate the depositions and statements of the accused with the investigation. For these purposes, I will ask the Prosecutor to supply us with all the testimonies. However, I do allow myself to call your attention to the fact that if - I do not want to prevent you from asking questions; of course, you can ask any questions you like - I do allow myself to recall that you pleaded guilty and that should you have the intention through the questions that you were asking that implicitly you were going to throw a question on the plea that you pleaded, it is now time to make this clear. But it would not be fair to the Prosecutor who has prepared himself according to certain types of procedures and not to another. This is the observation that I have, but of course I am not going to prevent you from asking the questions that you wish to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, I accept your objection but I have been taught by a principle that the confession of the accused does not always necessarily mean that - I just wanted that confession to be supported even more. That was my intention.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are still referring to the same question. We must be very clear. Are you - I am asking a question now - asking the Office of the Prosecutor to supply the results of the evaluations which are now in progress having to do with the human remains or traces of blood which were found in the municipal building? Are you asking for this report or not? If so, we must suspend for the hearing and wait for the observations of the Prosecutor or are you not asking this at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: Since the results are not yet known, I do not insist on that, but I just wanted to say that it would be good in support of the defence of my client, in support of his confession, to know them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: No, I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you any comments, Mr. Prosecutor, having to do with what was said by the Presiding Judge speaking to you and by Mr. Babic before I give my colleagues the opportunity to ask any questions they have? I give the floor to you now, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I turn to my colleagues. Judge Odio Benito, have you any questions you would like to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ruez, I would like to be sure about what you said here. You talked about Pilica school killings and you talked about Pilica farm killings. Could you explain to me the link between the Pilica school killings and the Pilica farm killings and the role played by Mr. Erdemovic in both situations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to be clear, I mentioned three situations. The first has to do with the events which took place in the Branjevo farm; facts, acts, rather, in which the accused has been a participant and for which he has pleaded guilty; then those that took place in a public building in Pilica, acts that he was a witness of which he reported to us and, last, acts which took place in the Pilica school about which Drazen Erdemovic does not know anything, which was a collection point for prisoners, where in fact there were murders committed, but which I did not mention at this point which made the made connection - in order to make the connection between this school and the Branjevo farm, which was also the point of execution for those prisoners that had been locked up in that school, had we not had Drazen Erdemovic's testimony, we would not have been able to discover through the investigation alone the place of the execution of those prisoners who had been locked up in the Pilica school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I heard you say, and I quote you, "Mr. Erdemovic was required to go to the Branjevo farm without knowing the nature of his mission". This statement is based on what? Is this your own judgment or are there any witnesses or is this the result of something he said to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I explained the situation that took place on the Branjevo farm, I was only giving a summary of these statements which Drazen Erdemovic made during the various discussions that we had together. I am only repeating his own words. At this point I have no way of confirming the correctness or the incorrectness of what he has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So this is not your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I had understood this is what you were stating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is the summary of the statements by Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Another question I would like to ask is that you stated that there were 500 prisoners locked up in the public building in Pilica, and then Mr. Erdemovic along with others refused to participate in their execution. Could you tell us what you are basing your statement on, which would allow you to say that he refused to do what he had been told to do or to go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first point has to do with the number of the prisoners. At this point we would have no way of checking or knowing independently what was the exact number of those persons locked up in that building. The only information that we do have about this has to do with something which was given to us by Erdemovic himself after the declarations that the Lieutenant Colonel on the Branjevo farm said who had told him to come and be a part of that execution. He is the one who told us the number of the people who were involved in this plan to execute people, about which during his declarations, during the discussions we had together, he states that he refused to participate in this. He says that he was the first to have opposed participating in that execution and that he was immediately followed by a certain number of his colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: This was stated by some of his colleagues as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was followed then, some of his colleagues refused after he did to participate in the execution. Now I am only repeating the statements that he made in the statement during the discussions that he had with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostberg, just a clarification: if you remember, you mentioned - I quote you - that the Prosecutor had no knowledge of the events prior to the confession of Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Which events are you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I am referring to the events that took place on the farm, on the killings, and from that we got also the information of the school and information about these killings in the town. As far as I recall from our investigation of what we have done in this case, the foundation for this information is the things we were told by Erdemovic. That is the only source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You had no clue when you were investigating the case of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever about this place. The name of the city or the environment of the city was not known to the Prosecutor as a site for execution before Erdemovic gave his statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I would like you to explain a bit more about the Sabotage Unit to which Drazen Erdemovic belonged. Did it consistent of volunteers? Was it a militia group? What is its status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This kind of Unit is found within each division of the Bosnian-Serb Army. The one Drazen Erdemovic belonged to is the 10th Sabotage Unit. It seems to be particular in the reports right back to central headquarters. So that is of direct relevance to our investigation, because it means that Drazen Erdemovic's information about events when it comes to the execution sites that they are so far north of the enclave shows the extent of the logistics necessary to carry out this kind of extermination operation as took place in July '95. Given the fact that these were sites, these were schools, it goes to show the organisation involved, the planning that was required for these executions. The Unit that Erdemovic belonged to gives an idea as to how the command was organised and how the executions were planned following the taking of Srebrenica. So that is something that is quite relevant in connection with his belonging to the Sabotage Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I had asked you whether it consisted of volunteers. Was this an elite Corps, these men specially trained or, in military terms, how would you assess it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can tell you about this unit is based on Drazen Erdemovic's statements. I do not know whether it is made up of volunteers or whether people were compelled to join it. Drazen Erdemovic only told us about his own situation. He said that he was driven to join the army with needing a salary and feeding his wife and child. He chose that Unit in so far as he said it consisted of elements, men, who were not all of Serb nationality. So, given his situation, that made life a little easier in that Unit because, on the basis of what he said, he was constantly worried about his safety because of his Croatian origin. So there were Serbian and Croats in this 10th Sabotage Unit, so he felt more at ease there than he would have in a Bosnian-Serb Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So what you are saying then is that he volunteered to be part of that Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of his statements, when he was on Republika Srpska territory for reasons he could best explain himself, he did volunteer to join the army. There was not a wide choice, but he did opt for the possibility of joining that Unit which, according to what he said, was a Unit that carried out sabotage operations in enemy territory.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any points that remain obscure as far as this investigation goes, that is to say, could you maybe list any points you have that are unclear in corroborating, as it were, Mr. Erdemovic's testimony? So are there any points which you think are of quite some significance and that call for some -

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my feeling is that as far as the topics go directly related to the investigation, Drazen Erdemovic has co- operated fully and comprehensively. I do not think that he kept any information away from us.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is something you might tell us later on. I know you are eager to do so. I would rather you did not answer that question right now. I have understood that the Office of the Prosecutor is quite content with Mr. Erdemovic's co-operation. My question is to you. You were in charge of the investigation about Srebrenica. As things now stand, are there any points that are obscure, that are contradictory, that you have not managed to clear up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no contradictions in what Drazen Erdemovic has said and what we have found independently in the course of the investigation. There is nothing that conflicts with what he has said. As regards all the topics we have broached, he has provided us with full information.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have one last question, and I am turning to Office of the Prosecutor. The Lieutenant Colonel was referred to. Is he at present being accused by the International Criminal Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has not yet been accused. The investigation in respect of the Lieutenant Colonel continues.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are there any other investigations under way as regards Drazen Erdemovic and his superiors? Are there any other investigations under way besides the one relating to the Lieutenant Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there certainly are. Our investigations are comprehensive. They will be in respect of all aspects relating to the summary executions at the Pilica farm and the hall, and other events described by Mr. Ruez in his initial summary of the events relating to the takeover of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Harmon, but I would like to insist on this now. I by no means want you to reveal investigations under way concerning other individuals, that is not the point here. We are trying a man for his involvement in specific acts and that is the Tribunal's mission, but it is also our mission to judge him on the basis of the role of his superiors. That is why I put the question to you about the Lieutenant Colonel. I think it would be very important for the Tribunal to know whether at present those investigations are under way and, in particular, as regards the Lieutenant Colonel as he has been identified by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my answer to that question is the same of course. Our investigation is focused on a number of higher ranking individuals responsible for the executions in and around Srebrenica and, in particular, the executions that occurred at Pilica farm and at the culture centre. One of the people we are investigating is the Lieutenant Colonel who has been mentioned by Mr. Erdemovic. So my answer is, yes, we do continue our investigations and, in particular, in relation to the Lieutenant Colonel we are attempting to investigate further his identity and elements relating to him.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall now proceed to a break and resume at 12 o'clock. At 12 o'clock we will hear what the Prosecution plans to submit in respect of the two witnesses. They will be protected, but there will also be questions from the Judges. Then there will also be the matter of deciding whether we will be hearing the accused Drazen Erdemovic. Then we will have to decide whether we will hear him right away or after the witnesses called by the Defence. We shall resume at 12 o'clock. 11.40 a.m. (The Court adjourned for a short time). 12.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We shall resume. Please have the accused shown in. The Chamber shall first of all hear from the Prosecutor's Office about the two witnesses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If I may recall Mr. Ruez to the stand. I propose that Mr. Ruez will give a summary to the Trial Chamber of what was said by two identified survivors of the massacre at the Pilica farm. I do not propose to have Mr. Ruez identify those survivors by name.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber - we had not yet taken a decision in fact, but since you were quite confident that we would give consent to your proposal, we are happy to welcome Mr. Ruez back. Now you are to give us a summary of the two testimonies, needless to say without identifying the persons involved. Subsequently, Mr. Babic, the Office of the Prosecutor and the Judges will be able to put questions to you. Please go ahead, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Ruez, has the Office of the Prosecutor identified two survivors from the massacre at Pilica farm on July 16th 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you please summarise for the Trial Chamber what they have informed the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the statements by these two persons to the Office of the Prosecutor, these two persons were amid the people in the Srebrenica enclave on 12th July 1995 when they were trying to get on to a bus that was evacuating them and their families towards the confrontation line, that is to say, towards Bosnian territory. They were separated. They were placed in a building in Potocari and from there they were evacuated with a group of prisoners towards Bratunac where they were locked up in what is referred to as the old Bratunac school which is a school that is behind the Vuk Karadzic school at Bratunac. While they were there they described the acts of violence that were perpetrated there against the other prisoners held. A lot of prisoners were beaten. Some of them were probably executed outside in so far as they could hear them yelling for help. Then they were shots that were heard and then there was silence. That went on for several days. Everyone was waiting for their own turn to be executed. Finally, on 15th July the prisoners who had not been killed near that school were evacuated, cleared from the building. They were loaded on to buses and the buses headed northwards, past Zvornik and they went to a school at the end of a dirt road. They gave a description of the place which enabled us subsequently, with further details they provided, to pinpoint the Pilica school as being the last place of their detention. When they reached the Pilica school there is the same treatment as the Bratunac school, that is to say, the prisoners were once again beaten. Some of them were taken outside by soldiers. They hear them screaming. They also hear the sound of gunfire shots. Once again, they think that their turn is coming. Then in the morning of 16th the soldiers who were guarding them tell them that they are going to be part of a prisoner exchange. They ask some of them to buy back their freedom, that if they have any money hidden on them to give it to them, and some prisoners do that. In the end all the prisoners have their hands tied behind their backs and by small groups they are loaded on the buses. The buses leave the Pilica school and take the dirt road that leads to a field that is just a few minutes away from where they were held. Once there the buses are guarded by two military policemen, that is for each bus. The prisoners were unloaded from the buses in small groups and led to the field. They can see that there are already bodies there lying scattered around. There is an execution squad that is set up behind them. So they line up in front of it and the execution squad starts firing at them. They were so fortunate as to survive that event. They were there amongst the bodies for the remainder of the afternoon. They waited for sunset to crawl to freedom and they headed off to where they were intercepted by a patrol. Then they were taken to Zvornik and put into a prisoner camp. They were registered there by the Red Cross and subsequently exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, from what you have told us, if I have understood rightly, it is a school, it is an execution in the school that we are referring to. Do you have similar chronological information about what happened at the Branjevo farm where the accused was present as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with regard to the Branjevo farm events that have already been outlined, the scenario is quite similar to how the survivors said things happened and the details as to the violence there has also been set forth by Drazen Erdemovic, the fact that those injured were left to suffer, that they were then executed individually if they gave any signs of life. So it was quite savage the way the perpetrators behaved. We have the same information from the survivors and Drazen Erdemovic. So that goes for Banjevo farm as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, but do you have any more detailed information, in particular as regards the participation of Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None of the survivors were able to identify anyone. They had to look down. If they looked up they were beaten and subjected even to being executed right there if they tried to see what was going on around them. They cannot formally identify the farm for the same reasons, which makes it quite likely that these people survived the same events as described by Drazen Erdemovic. It is the same date, 16th July. They were already there the day before. If the executions did take place nearby, given the large numbers involved, they would have heard the events happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What about the measures taken before the executions, the torture, the means used? Do you have more information about how the prisoners were treated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the events in situ as I outlined, the savage behaviour on the part of the perpetrators, the executions as have been reported by the various parties. There is nothing I can add to that, unless you want me to go into great deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: About the savage behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, as Drazen Erdemovic has said, initially things were fairly well organised. The prisoners were brought before the firing squad. They were executed but, little by little, Drazen Erdemovic's mates, as it were, start drinking. They do not have the patience. They cannot wait for the military police to unload people. They charged the buses. They hit the prisoners with iron bars and beat some of them. They humiliate their victims, they insult them. All of these acts have also been described by the survivors. Now individual executions, because after the process of execution the perpetrators checked to see whether anyone is still alive and there is then an individual killing, that is if anyone is alive, and what was said corresponds in both cases. The executions, the collective executions, that we have dealt with in the course of the investigation revealed a similar scenario. There is an execution, a general execution and then there is a check to see that everyone is indeed dead. Then there is a fairly quick execution of any survivors, etc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So what the survivors have said and what Mr. Erdemovic has said is more or less identical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no major differences and there is no reason, therefore, to believe that what has been said is untrue. So one can take it that both parties are sincere in what they said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there a direct superior of Mr. Erdemovic who was in control of the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the names of the perpetrators have already been stated in the course of this public hearing in July. Drazen Erdemovic has always given the name of the participants in the atrocities, that is to say, he has given the names of his fellow soldiers, the names of the people who ever participated in the atrocities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What about superiors, did he tell you who his superiors were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he gave the name of the leader of the execution squad as well as the names of the seven other members of the Unit. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 161 to 173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The head of that Unit, where is he? What do we know about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He should still be at Bijeljina right now.
